precepts.text: They that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare. The love of money is the root of all evil, which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith and pierced themselves through with many sorrows. That is what Satan will have you do. If you covet fame and fortune in this world, you must worship Satan; that is the only way.
precepts.point: And the dragon, which is Satan in this part right here, gave him his power, his armaments, and his seat, and great authority.
precepts.why:
Satan's stipulation is worship, and many of our people will pay it for money. Paul says, “But they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition.”

“For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.”

That is what Satan will have you do: pierce yourself through with many sorrows, because you covet to be rich in this world. If you covet fame and fortune in this world, you must worship Satan. You must; that is the only way. That is what the Bible is saying.

So the power and the seat and great authority that the dragon gave the beast in Revelation 13 is the same thing he offered Christ on the mountain, all the kingdoms of the world and the glory of them, and the price has always been the same: fall down and worship me. The ones who will be rich take that snare and err from the faith.

precepts.text: Our people don't want to be content with the love of the Lord; they want to be rich. There's all these contracts out there for entertainers; there's always a catch-22, that gotcha moment, which drown men in destruction and perdition. For the love of money is the root of all evil. So when you're asked to work seven days a week or work on the Sabbath, don't call us and say, hey, is it okay if I break the Sabbath? We're going to tell you no. We're not going to tell you to break God's laws; that's between you and the Lord. Don't involve us in your trial.
precepts.point: That verse speaks volumes. Deceivableness: the easy word is deceit. Unrighteousness: sin. All deceit of sin, breaking God's laws. In them that perish, because they received not the love of the truth: this is about our people.
precepts.why:
“But they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition.” Our people don't want to be content with the love of the Lord; they want to be rich. There are all these contracts out there for entertainers, and there's always a catch-22, that gotcha moment, the snare that drowns men in destruction and perdition.

Look at Brandon Tatum: that verse fits him 100%. They raise him up politically, while, as the lady said at the beginning, Trump got rid of all those black leaders in the government. Look at Get Out, the scene where they were bidding. We thought it was just a movie, but the Edomite at the beginning said, we do talk about y'all. Where are we going to put you? Who's going into what sport? We bid on you. That's what they do.

“For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.” So when you're asked to work seven days a week or work on the Sabbath, don't call us and say, hey, is it okay if I break the Sabbath? We're going to tell you no. We're not going to tell you to break God's laws; that's between you and the Lord. Don't involve us in your trial.

The love of money is the love they took in place of the love of the truth, and it drowns them in perdition.

precepts.text: Let as many servants as are under the yoke count their own masters worthy of all honour. And they that have believing masters, let them not despise them, because they are brethren. Not one time does the Lord say we are brethren with the other nations, so those masters are Israelites. If your master still believed in the law of sacrifice but you believed on Christ, you still honored him and treated him with respect.
precepts.point: Masters, give unto your servants that which is just and equal. They claimed they were the masters; did they do that? No. They lived in the big house while we lived in the outhouse, and we never got the forty acres and the mule. So they showed themselves hypocrites and impostors. The verse ends: knowing that ye also have a Master in heaven.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
Paul elaborates on the masters: “Let as many servants as are under the yoke count their own masters worthy of all honour, that the name of God and his doctrine be not blasphemed.” The servants are under the yoke, the yoke of bondage. If you had a master who still believed in the law of sacrifice, but you believed on Christ, you still honoured him. He follows sacrifice, but you still treat him with respect.

“And they that have believing masters, let them not despise them, because they are brethren”. Now you have Israelite masters who believe on Christ. Don’t despise a master, your brother, that believes on Christ, because they are brethren.

Not one time has the Lord ever said we are brothers with the other nations. So that is showing you those masters are Israelites. When Colossians 4:1 tells masters to give their servants what is just and equal, it is speaking to Israelite masters over Israelite servants, their brethren.

precepts.text: Every wise woman buildeth her house: but the foolish plucketh it down with her hands. Instead of watching what that other husband is doing, study that wise woman. Go ask her: what are you doing? Why is he so happy? Every time you ask for something, he gives it; what is the secret? She has a mind to what is going on in her house: these are the things I need to fix to make my household better, this is how I assist my husband. That is the desire of Genesis: she shall desire her husband. That means studying him: you know what he likes, his dislikes, when to leave him be, and when to come speak. But pride, sister, will keep you from doing it. You think he is supposed to give you everything first before you do what you do as a wife; that is not what you are in the marriage for. You do your job, and that man does his job. And if reciprocation only flows one way, you might be the reason your marriage is the way it is.
precepts.point: Which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith. And a lot of you women in marriages covet other people's marriages based on what they have. You see somebody else with a big house and feel your marriage is inadequate; they got a new car, they go on trips, why are we not doing that? But what are you doing to fix the things in your own marriage? You do not know what they have been through: they may have struggled fifteen or twenty years before any financial establishment came into that relationship. You see the here and now, not the hardships and the pain on the way. You think the grass is greener, and you do not know what happens in that house at night. When you desire what another man is doing in his house, you are coveting, breaking the ten commandments.
precepts.why:
“which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith”. A lot of sisters in marriages covet other people's marriages: he's doing this, he's doing that, and you're mad at your husband because he isn't doing what that brother is doing, when he is probably trying to get where he needs to be. Solomon points you somewhere else: “Every wise woman buildeth her house”.

You're looking at the wrong thing. Instead of watching what that husband is doing, study her. Why don't you go ask her: what are you doing? What's the secret? Why is he so happy? Every time you ask for something he gives it; I see you with the new purse, the new shoes. Ask her how she's building her house up.

The wise woman has a mind to what is going on in the house: these are the things I need to fix to make my household better; this is how I assist my husband. That is why Genesis says her desire shall be to her husband. It means you study him: you know his likes and dislikes, what irritates him, when not to mess with him, and when to come say something. You live in the house; you see it all the time.

“but the foolish plucketh it down with her hands.” Your pride, sister, will keep you from doing it. You think he's supposed to give you everything first before you get on board: if he ain't doing this for me, I ain't doing nothing for him. You're out of your damn mind; that isn't what you're in the marriage for. He is out providing, bringing food into the house, clothes for the kids, paying the bills. You do your job and he does his. If he has to do it all before you reciprocate anything, something's wrong, and you might be the reason your marriage is the way it is.

precepts.text: Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life. You cannot fight that fight without holding to your profession.
precepts.point: There is no perfect sister; this is a hospital and all of us are sick, and Christ came for those who admit it. Sisters who complain that another sister has an attitude need a solution, not a grievance, and patience. And when you fall, get back up; the righteous fall seven times. Where would you go, back to white Jesus? Leaders, do not kick a brother when he is down or take revenge on a brother who lost rank; build him back up.

note.label: Dark Places of the Heart: the Hidden Cost of Sin

precepts.why:
“Seeing then that we have a great high priest, that is passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast our profession.” What is our profession? We are prophets, and a prophet’s profession is to teach. All of us are supposed to be teachers. Timothy gives the charge: “Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses.”

You cannot get that eternal life if you do not hold on to your profession. How are you going to fight the good fight of faith if you are not holding on to it? Your profession is to go out there and wake up our people. Your profession is to put in work, because faith without works is dead. Your first work is supposed to be in this truth, not your job. The minute we say profession, some think we mean I’m a nurse, I’m a doctor. No.

What good is it for a prophet to do nothing with it? Some of you never travel, never leave the state of Georgia, yet you say I’m a prophet. All Israel is not in Georgia; Israel is scattered to the four corners of the earth. How many of you prophets have a valid passport? Brothers have had passports since they were three. If you don’t have one, you should be ashamed. Get a passport; Donald Trump is going to force you to get one too. We have much work to do.

And “all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do.” God will bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good or evil. So hold fast the profession, fight the fight, and lay hold on eternal life with a high priest who was “in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin.”

precepts.text: Fight the good fight of faith; lay hold on eternal life as Jacob laid hold until he was blessed.
precepts.point: That is the spirit to carry through hardship: fight the good fight of faith and lay hold on eternal life the way Jacob laid hold and would not let go.
precepts.why:
“Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called”.

Jacob laid hold and would not let go. With his thigh out of joint he still said, “I will not let thee go, except thou bless me.” That is faith with works, and it is the spirit to carry through hardship: fight the good fight of faith and lay hold on eternal life the way Jacob laid hold until he was blessed.

precepts.text: Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses.
precepts.point: The work of the Lord is the true calling over any occupation held in Babylon: consider the Apostle and High Priest of our profession, Christ Jesus; fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses.
precepts.why:
“Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses.”

Pharaoh laid more work upon the men so that they would not regard vain words, and this captivity does the same, dangling extra wages for working the Sabbath and the feast days. The good profession, professed before many witnesses, is the work of the Lord, the true calling over any occupation held in Babylon; fight the good fight of faith and lay hold on eternal life rather than the taskmaster's wages.

precepts.text: The rich are charged to be ready to distribute, willing to communicate; the law of the gleanings teaches the same giving.
precepts.point: Charge them that are rich that they be not highminded, but ready to distribute, willing to communicate. Most of us today have no fields or vineyards, but some have good jobs and blessed incomes; you cannot take it with you, so give of your substance. The scriptures also say no good can come to him that gives no alms.

note.label: Leviticus 19: Ye Shall Be Holy, for I the Lord Your God Am Holy

precepts.why:
“Charge them that are rich in this world, that they be not highminded, nor trust in uncertain riches, but in the living God”; “That they do good, that they be rich in good works, ready to distribute, willing to communicate.” The law of the gleanings teaches the same giving.

Most of us today have no fields or vineyards, but some have good jobs and blessed incomes. You cannot take it with you, so give of your substance. The scriptures also say no good can come to him that gives no alms.

precepts.text: The love of money is the root of all evil; the gold that Gideon gathered turned into the very snare that trapped his own house.
precepts.point: Gideon made an ephod thereof and put it in his city, even in Ophrah: and all Israel went thither a whoring after it, which thing became a snare unto Gideon, and to his house.

note.label: Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal

precepts.why:
“For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.”

Gideon gathered “a thousand and seven hundred shekels of gold” in earrings, “beside ornaments, and collars, and purple raiment that was on the kings of Midian, and beside the chains that were about their camels’ necks.” He made an ephod of it and put it in Ophrah, “and all Israel went thither a whoring after it: which thing became a snare unto Gideon, and to his house.” The gold that Gideon gathered turned into the very snare that trapped his own house; he pierced himself through with many sorrows.

precepts.text: Charge them that are rich not to be high-minded nor trust in uncertain riches but in the living God who giveth us richly all things to enjoy.
precepts.point: Riches are uncertain; money in an online bank cannot be reached when Wi-Fi and electricity go out, and then the rich man is in the same boat as the poor.

note.label: Psalm 49: The Vanity of Riches Against the Grave

precepts.why:
Paul gives the charge: “Charge them that are rich in this world, that they be not highminded, nor trust in uncertain riches, but in the living God, who giveth us richly all things to enjoy”. That is the answer to the ones in Psalm 49 who “trust in their wealth, and boast themselves in the multitude of their riches”. Riches are uncertain. Money sitting in an online bank cannot be reached when the Wi-Fi and the electricity go out, and then the rich man is in the same boat as the poor man.

Many of Israel's own brothers and sisters trust in their riches. The charge to them is the same: be not high-minded, do not trust in uncertain riches, trust in the living God, the one who gives us richly all things to enjoy.

moments.label: Covetous Eyes Will Be Put Out

points: Money. For the love of money is the root of all evil. Why is money the root? Because money brings all those other elements you deal with to the surface. With money comes attention, power, respect, desirability; that is what people desire in America, rather than to be viewed with righteousness: this is a good brother, he is loyal, he reasons with you with the scriptures, he gives good and wise counsel. That is what you want to be remembered as. But a lot of you have made money your god.

Which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith. And a lot of you women in marriages covet other people's marriages based on what they have. You see somebody else with a big house and feel your marriage is inadequate; they got a new car, they go on trips, why are we not doing that? But what are you doing to fix the things in your own marriage? You do not know what they have been through: they may have struggled fifteen or twenty years before any financial establishment came into that relationship. You see the here and now, not the hardships and the pain on the way. You think the grass is greener, and you do not know what happens in that house at night. When you desire what another man is doing in his house, you are coveting, breaking the ten commandments.

They that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition. Ye said if you ever see a video of me with a goat, he knew what he did to get where he is and they dangle it over his head. They have something on all of them. Our people in entertainment can repent, but they fear the public humiliation of what they did for their fortunes.

The love of money, not money itself, is the root of all evil, which while some coveted after they have erred from the faith and pierced themselves through with many sorrows. Covetousness is the last commandment and starts in the mind; if you covet you will steal, if you steal you will lie, and then you will murder, a domino effect. A young lady from our Houston school went on America's Next Top Model and cried that her friends said the white man was a devil but she did not believe it; to get the contract she had to cast her bowels.

But thou, O man of God, flee these things. There is nothing wrong with better jobs and higher education, but when you covet money you are going about it in a spiritually disastrous way. Follow after righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, meekness; fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life.
Godliness with contentment is great gain. We brought nothing into this world and carry nothing out; you leave with a garment and a coffin, so why ruin eternal life over money, cars and houses?

note.label: Covetous Eyes Will Be Put Out

points: Having food and raiment, let us be therewith content. They that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, into foolish and hurtful lusts which drown men in destruction. Get rich or die trying means you will die.

note.label: Covetous Eyes Will Be Put Out

points: The love of money is the root of all evil. If you will rob, steal and lie for it, you will kill for it, and defrauding your brother is hatred. Most brothers here are broke, so why defraud a brother who is broke like you? And do not cozy up to the few who have money because they have it.

Some coveted after money and pierced themselves through with many sorrows. A good name is rather to be chosen than riches, and once your name is mud over money nobody will deal with you again. Some brothers should not be in business at all; a covetous man's business will not prosper except in unrighteousness.

note.label: Covetous Eyes Will Be Put Out

points: Godliness with contentment is great gain. We carry nothing out of this world.
They that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and the love of money is the root of all evil. A job that takes the Sabbath is not worth your rank or your soul.
Fight the good fight of faith and lay hold on eternal life. Faith is the pattern.
